extraction.description: The concept type that the extracted string denotes does not match the evaluated attribute at all. This can be judged purely from the attribute name and the extracted string in isolation, without needing to read the BioSample metadata for context: would this string plausibly be the right kind of entity for this attribute at all, ignoring whether the specific role/status holds? Examples include extracting a drug or other treatment reagent as knockout_gene (not a gene at all, so this is a type mismatch even though 'knockout' also does not apply), a tissue name as disease, a disease mention as cell_type or tissue, or a treatment reagent as disease.

The concept type that the extracted string denotes does match the evaluated attribute, but the extracted string plays the wrong role or belongs to the wrong sub-classification within that type. Judging this requires reading the BioSample metadata for context, not just the attribute name and extracted string in isolation. Examples include extracting a ChIP target, assay target, antibody target, transgene, or measured gene as knockout_gene, knockdown_gene, or overexpressed_gene when the metadata shows it was not actually knocked out, knocked down, or overexpressed; or extracting a stem cell line or other source cell line mentioned in the metadata as cell_line when the actual sample is a differentiated cell derived from that cell line rather than the original cell line itself.

The extraction used the wrong text boundary, such as taking only part of a composite expression or including extra words, causing the extracted value to mean something different from the BioSample metadata.
The extracted string does not appear as a substring in any of the BioSample attributes, Ids, description, or title, and appears to be generated through hallucination.

The BioSample metadata itself is ambiguous, contradictory, or too underspecified for reliable interpretation, even for a human reviewer. Examples include different plausible cell line names appearing in different metadata fields, such as source_name and cell line, without enough context to tell which one represents the sample itself.
The extracted value is appropriate for the evaluated attribute.
